title: Studying the Universe
caption: The Unit Telescopes of the Very Large Telescope under a clear sky, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope stand beneath a clear night sky at Paranal Observatory. Each one carries its own set of instruments.

Every instrument is custom-made for one way of studying the Universe and aimed at a different scientific question. Taken together, the VLT's instrument programme is described as the most ambitious ever planned for a single observatory, covering all the main observing modes needed for most of today's leading research.

This well-equipped facility has opened a new age of discovery. Among its achievements are some notable astronomical firsts, including the first image of a planet outside our Solar System and the tracking of stars as they swing near the supermassive black hole in our galaxy's core.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so faint stars appear brighter and more numerous than they would to someone standing there.

explore: The photograph was taken by Daniele Gasparri. Because each Unit Telescope hosts a different set of purpose-built instruments, the VLT as a whole can study the Universe in many different ways and take on a wide range of questions.
